newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds jump on short-covering in New York.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds jump on short-covering in New York.

text.p: Argentine bonds jumped early Wednesday on short-covering by investors in New York, traders said.
"Apparently there are many shorts on the FRB," said a trader at a large foreign bank. The local market shot up on the higher FRB.
The 5.5 percent dollar-denominated Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 rose $0.50 to 117.85. The "Pre 2" hit a high of 118.0 in the morning. Argentina's FRB due 2005 rose 6/8 to 81-1/8.
Another trader said the sharp rise in the market came on the back of foreign buying. He added that there was no news that had fuelled the surge.
But the market was waiting for Congress' debate on the government's tax-hiking measures Wednesday. The debate is not expected until late in the day.
Even if the measures are passed as is expected, the part of the plan which would give central government a larger portion of the revenues from petrol taxes is not seen being passed this session.

Even so, Congress approval of the measures could ensure that a letter of intent with the International Monetary Fund will be signed before the weekend, including a budget deficit target of $5 billion for this year. Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said Tuesday he expected the letter of intent signed before the weekend.
